text: Entry 2071 clones a cached select statement before binding folder ID. MessageEnumerator owns that clone, advances it after each returned header and finalizes it on destruction. Separate instances must not share cursor position or bindings. Reverse enumeration has ORDER BY id DESC; forward enumeration lacks an explicit ORDER BY, so the fixture’s ascending result is not a general SQL ordering rule. The 2072 test enumerates keys and subjects twice to require a fresh instance. Shared cleanup clears references and forces GC so destructors can finalize statements after failures. Proposed additional checks are interleaved folders, early termination and ExecuteStep errors. No runtime or failure experiment ran.
title: Each Panorama message enumerator owns a cloned SQL cursor
